2. The petitioner as plaintiff instituted the suit against opposite party No. 1 The opposite party No. 2 on his own representation was added as defendant No. 2 in the said suit and others were impleaded as proforma-defendants by the plaintiff. The suit was for declaration of title in the land in suit on the ground that ROR Khatian was erroneously recorded in the name of the Government of Bangladesh, opposite party No. 1. The case of the plaintiff was, in short, that land in suit originally belonged to Zaminder Brajendra Kishore Roy Chowdhury from whom plaintiffs father Jaha Box Bepari took jote pattan an 25th Bhadra, 1351 BS at a rental of Taka 6.00 on payment of najar selami. He got possession of the same on assertion of his title to the knowledge of all. Jaha Box died leaving plaintiff-petitioner as a son and proforma defendant Nos. 3-8 as other heirs. On amicable arrangement with the other heirs of Jaha Box the plaintiff alone got the land in suit and was in exclusive possession therein. His further case was that in the middle part of Falgoon, 1387 BS he learnt for the first time the wrong recording of the land in suit in the name of the Government. Hence the suit. 

 6. Mr. Mohammad Ali further contended that the Court of appeal below seriously committed mistake in law leading to mistake in his decision occasioning failure of justice in holding only upon the finding of a rent receipt that it was written on an old form and the signature of the grantor and the serial number of the rent receipt are over-written which create suspicion for holding that the rent receipts are not genuine. He submits that when there are three dakhilas of the sheresta of ex-landlord-one for 1351 BS, another for 1354 BS and another for 1357 BS it was not permissible on the part of the Court of appeal below, merely on overwriting of the dakhila of 1354 BS, to hold that all other dakhilas are not genuine. He submitted that the settlement was taken on payment of rent as per dakhilas, Exhibits-1 series, in particular dakhila for the year 1351 BS and not by adverse possession. The Additional District Judge misdirected himself in holding on conjecture that "the question of acquiring title by adverse possession does not stand as the land was found in Zaminder's khas in 1954". In that the finding is contrary to the concurrent finding that "all these prove the long possession of the plaintiff". Thus, this finding of the Court of appeal below, as contended by Mr. AJ Mohammad Ali, disclosed that the land in question was Zaminder's khas land in 1954 as found by the lower appellate Court. He further argued that in absence of gazette notification ex-landlord and absence of the original rent roll assessment of the khas land of the landlord, the Court of appeal below accepting the original volume of compensation assessment roll produced, erroneously held that compensation assessment roll prepared in 1954 when 3.36 acres of land including the suit land was still in khas possession of the landlord, inasmuch as the Court of appeal below did not notice that the volume produced was contrary to the concurrent findings that the suit land was in possession of the father of the plaintiff since 1351 BS and, as such, such preparation of compensation assessment roll was fabricated.
